notes: Medium. The agent must build a reusable eval harness (strict 3-arg CLI, exact metric semantics including the UNKNOWN-never-fabricates rule, outputs that must equal an independent scorer of the same deterministic model to 1e-6) that reproduces a documented prompt trade-off (v1 0.60/0.00 -> v2 0.97/0.19) from raw measurements over the 200-record shipped set, then write a third prompt version that clears a declared bar on BOTH metrics (ref_acc >= 0.95, fabrication_rate <= 0.03) and prove it in a shipped eval report. Difficulty comes from debugging_ambiguity: the agent must diagnose by measurement which prompt trait drives each metric (canonical-normalization wording drives ref accuracy; carrier-completion guidance drives the fabrication regression; the model card documents the later-instruction-wins override), and then decide how to keep normalization while neutralizing the guidance -- the instruction withholds the v3 recipe and only a prompt that gets both traits right clears the bar on the fresh sets too. reasoning_depth (2): distinguishing the two traits and tracing fabrications to their prompt cause. hidden_case_generalization (2): the verifier re-runs the harness on 3 fresh record sets plus a gold-mutated synthetic set with independent re-scoring on every run, so canned or hardcoded numbers fail. The indifference-zone tolerance (v3 within 2pp of v2's ref_rate and within 3pp of v1's fabrication rate, in the better direction; ref_acc >= 0.95; fabrication_rate <= 0.03) is declared up front and can only be met by a genuinely better prompt, never by trimming the bar.
